question: Who among the following compiled the Mriga-Pasi-Shastra in the 13th century, which gave details of animals and birds of prey?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hansdev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mriga-Pasi-Shastra:** The **Mriga-Pasi-Shastra** was a text compiled in the **13th century** and is an important work in the field of zoology and hunting practices in medieval India. It provides detailed accounts of various **animals** and **birds of prey**.
 
• **Hansdev:** The Mriga-Pasi-Shastra was compiled by **Hansdev**. He is recognized as a significant figure in documenting information about animals and birds, including their behaviors and characteristics, during the 13th century.
 
• The text is one of the early Indian works that contributed to the field of **natural history**, focusing on the **classification and study of animals** in a scientific manner.
 
• The purpose of this compilation was not only to describe animal behavior but also to serve as a guide for **hunters and naturalists** of that era.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Hansdev and His Contribution:**

 
 
• Hansdev was a prominent scholar and naturalist in the **13th century**.
 
• He is renowned for his work, the **Mriga-Pasi-Shastra**, which remains a significant document in the study of animals and birds, especially in the context of hunting and observing their natural behaviors.
 
• The text showcases the knowledge and interest in zoology during medieval India and is a reflection of the intellectual pursuits of the time.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Akbar:** Akbar was the Mughal emperor of India (1556–1605) known for his administrative reforms and cultural patronage. He was not associated with the Mriga-Pasi-Shastra, but he did have a keen interest in animals and maintained a vast collection of animals in his royal court.
 
• **Jahangir:** Jahangir, Akbar’s son, was another Mughal emperor known for his love of nature and wildlife. He maintained records of flora and fauna and even ordered paintings of animals and birds during his reign, but he did not compile the Mriga-Pasi-Shastra.
 
• **Mansoor:** Mansoor was a famous Mughal court painter during the reign of Jahangir. He was renowned for his realistic paintings of animals and birds, but he did not contribute to the creation of the Mriga-Pasi-Shastra.
 
 
 
• **Medieval Indian Contributions to Zoology:**
 
 
• Medieval Indian scholars, including Hansdev, made significant contributions to the study of flora and fauna through their detailed observations and writings.
 
• Such works highlight the rich knowledge base of ancient and medieval Indian scholars in the field of natural sciences.
 
• The Mriga-Pasi-Shastra is a prime example of how ancient Indian texts documented the behavior, characteristics, and utility of various animal species.
